newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian shares look down on domestic sales.
newsitem.headline: Russian shares look down on domestic sales.

text.p: Leading Russian shares sank in early trade on Wednesday as domestic operators sold stocks on sporadic profit-taking as recent gains appear to have stalled for now, traders said, predicting the market would ease further.

"There have been sales since this morning, mostly Russian, but some Western investors, although I wouldn't say there was a significant amount of paper thrown on to the market," said Aton trader Alexander Bobolev.
"I think the blue-chip market is overall geared to drop a little bit lower."
The Russian Trading System 22-share index edged down to 355.13 at opening after 355.30 on Tuesday.
But Dmitry Starenko, vice-president of Regent European Securities said he did not see the consolidation was a result of any particular events.
"Some people just see that the market is not growing and are lightening their books," Starenko said.
National electricity company UES was $0.3112 at 0925 GMT after closing on Tuesday at $0.3170, while natural gas producer Gazprom fell to $0.625 from $0.653.

Traders said the decline in Gazprom price, after several days of consistent growth and the release of positive 1996 financial results, was due to market rumours of a draft decree by the president limiting non-resident trade in Gazprom shares.
A Gazprom spokesman declined to comment, saying that he did not know "which version of the existing ones will be signed".
Regent's Starenko said the information was overshadowing Gazprom's announcement that its 1996 pre-tax profit rose to 45.09 trillion roubles from 19.64 trillion roubles in 1995.
"Everyone started selling Gazprom yesterday evening," he said. "The market reacted very naturally, as it would to any kind of limitation or change in the rules of play."
But ING Bank trader Oleg Galkin said the good financials could balance the rumours about a decree.

He said the market would fluctuate around current levels for the next few days on weak interest from Western investors, who he said had still not decided on strategy after the Federal Reserve left U.S. interest rates untouched earlier this month.
